name: Maserati F136 YG 4.7 L V8 (Quattroporte S, 2008-2010)
summary: The long-stroke 4.7 L version of the Maserati cross-plane F136, with a 60-degree intake cam phaser; 430 CV (425 hp US) at 7000 rpm and 490 N m at 4750 in the Quattroporte S.

variant.value: F136 YG, Quattroporte S (M139 R / M139IQ), 2008-2010
variant.note: Academy p. 15 MY09 M139 range: 'Quattroporte S (M139IQ) 430 [HP] 4.7 automatic YG'. Chosen over the Sport GT S (F136 YH, 440 HP) because the Quattroporte S has the standard exhaust; the Sport GT S's bypass-valve silencers and filterless intake are things this model cannot switch. Wikipedia lists F136 YG for the Quattroporte S 2008-2010.

compression_ratio.note: p. 226, Quattroporte S: '11.02'. The Academy gives 11.25:1 for the F136 YK (GranTurismo MC Stradale), a different variant.

firing_order.note: p. 226 'Ignition sequence: 1-8-6-2-7-3-4-5', listed for both versions. Inference, not read on a page: the manuals give the order but no cylinder-numbering diagram was opened. Numbering is taken as 1-4 on one bank and 5-8 on the other, front to back. This is the only common numbering under which 1-8-6-2-7-3-4-5 is a valid cross-plane order (each bank then fires at 90-180-270-180, and cylinders n and n+4 share a crank pin); with alternating numbering (odd one bank, even the other) the order would put three consecutive firings on one bank. Which bank is 1-4 is not known and does not change the model.

crank.note: As for the 4.2: Wikipedia F136 infobox; consistent with the factory firing order. Also stated for the Quattroporte V specifically: Wikipedia, Maserati Quattroporte (fifth-generation section): the Quattroporte V's F136 engines had 'a crossplane crankshaft, four valves per cylinder driven by two overhead camshafts per bank and continuous variable valve timing on the intake side'; F136S in DuoSelect cars, dry sump.

cam_timing_check.value: intake valve lift 0.60 +/- 0.08 mm at 25 deg after TDC; exhaust valve lift 0.60 +/- 0.08 mm at TDC
cam_timing_check.note: Academy p. 15 (also pp. 27, 30, 38), F136 YG. Workshop cam-setting values, not durations; reading the intake value as the phaser's rest position is ours. Read from the Wayback Machine copy http://web.archive.org/web/20220327103955/https://academy.maserati.com/wbt/upload/lmsIveco-1564/011704-Product_Update_Course_EN.pdf (original host refused connections).

variable_valve_timing.value: intake cams only, continuously variable, 60 crank degrees (30 cam degrees)
variable_valve_timing.note: Academy p. 13: 'The F136YG and F136YH engines of the Quattroporte S and Quattroporte Sport GT S are equipped with new valve timing control devices allowing total timing variation of 30 (60 engine actuation).' Intake-only is also stated for the Quattroporte V's engines by Wikipedia, Maserati Quattroporte (fifth-generation section): the Quattroporte V's F136 engines had 'a crossplane crankshaft, four valves per cylinder driven by two overhead camshafts per bank and continuous variable valve timing on the intake side'; F136S in DuoSelect cars, dry sump.

redline_rpm.note: Academy p. 15 (MY09 Quattroporte, ZF 6HP26 section): 'peak power available up to the highest engine speeds (7,600 rpm)'. Taken as the rev limit; that reading is ours.

peak_power_kw.note: p. 226, 'Maximum power (EC) kW 317, HP 425' at 7,000 r.p.m. (US manual). The Academy and Wikipedia give 430 HP/PS (316 kW).

peak_torque_nm.note: p. 226, 'Maximum torque (EC) Nm 490, kgm 50' at 4,750 r.p.m. Wikipedia and Autozine (361 lbft) agree.

intake_type.note: Not found. The Academy says the Sport GT S differs from the Quattroporte S by 'a modification to the intake and exhaust system', with no filter on the air-flow meter, but does not describe the manifold.

exhaust_notes.value: standard exhaust without bypass valves; quad round tailpipes
exhaust_notes.note: Academy p. 14: the Sport GT S, 'like the GranTurismo S', has a racing exhaust with bypass valves in the rear silencers; this is not said of the Quattroporte S (that the S has none is our reading). Quad round tailpipes: Wikipedia, Maserati Quattroporte. Manifold layout, crossover and pipe sizes not found.

missing: intake runner length, diameter and plenum
header type, primary and secondary dimensions, crossover

sources.what: Maserati Quattroporte owner's manual, US edition, M139 (book dated 1 September 2008, 2009 model year), hosted by the Maserati Club UK (a ManualsLib download). Manufacturer document: technical specifications p. 226 for the 4.2 (M139 A) and 4.7 (M139 R) versions.

Maserati Academy, 'Maserati Range Technical Updates', July 2012, training documentation for the Maserati service network (cited by Wikipedia's F136 article). Read from the Wayback Machine copy http://web.archive.org/web/20220327103955/https://academy.maserati.com/wbt/upload/lmsIveco-1564/011704-Product_Update_Course_EN.pdf because the original host refused connections; manufacturer document.
Wikipedia, Ferrari F136 engine: variant table (engine codes, years, power, torque, sump type) sourced to the Maserati Academy, and the cross-plane statement.
Autozine (Mark Wan), Quattroporte V review: Quattroporte S 430 hp at 7000 rpm, 361 lbft at 4750 rpm.

Wikipedia, Maserati Quattroporte: fifth-generation engine paragraph (cross-plane crank, intake-side continuous variable valve timing, F136S dry sump in DuoSelect cars); quad round tailpipes on the standard cars; Sport GT S bypass-valve exhaust.

name.note: US owner's manual, M139, 2009 model year, covering the Quattroporte (4.2) and Quattroporte S (4.7, F136 YG).

curb_kg.note: p.231. Quote: "Empty vehicle weight (with tanks filled, tools and accessories) 4,425 lb (2.010 kg)", same for both versions. No driver.

gear_count.note: p.227. Quote: "Six forward speeds and one reverse."

gears.note: p.227. Quote: "1st gear 4.171 14.77 / 2nd gear 2.340 8.28 / 3rd gear 1.521 5.38 / 4th gear 1.143 4.05 / 5th gear 0.867 3.07 / 6th gear 0.691 2.45" (gearbox ratio, total reduction).

final_drive.note: p.228. Quote: "Differential reduction ratio 13/46 = 3.54". Consistent with the total reductions above (4.171 x 3.54 = 14.77).

tyre.note: p.229, rear. Quote: "rear ... 10.5”J x 19” (+) 285/35 ZR19"; the S column lists only 19 and 20 inch, both marked "+ Wheel rims available on request". Taking 19 inch as standard is our inference (smallest S size).

wheel_radius_m.note: Estimated (ours): rolling radius taken as 98% of the unloaded radius computed from the tyre size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio).

top_speed_kmh.note: p.231. Quote: "Maximum speed ... Version Quattroporte S ... 280 174" (km/h, mph).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Maserati Quattroporte' (read 2026-11-17), infobox fifth generation (Pininfarina, Ken Okuyama) layout: Front-mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive.
